adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — The acting user's credentials (which may be a mere attendee's) are used to build EventManager and mutate the organizer's calendar, so a side effect fires under the wrong identity.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, permission allows an attendee to call this mutation (`const isAttendee = ...` and the `FORBIDDEN` check). But the calendar mutation is executed via `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`, where `user` is the acting user from `ctx`, not the booking organizer. That `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` therefore runs under the attendee’s credentials/identity, even though `evt.organizer` is derived from the booking’s organizer. This is exactly the “side effect under the wrong identity” problem described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52 — Any attendee may add further guests, who then become attendees and can add more, giving self-propagating spam amplification sent from the organizer's domain.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the permission check explicitly allows any existing attendee (`isAttendee`) to call the `addGuests` mutation: `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) ...` (around the referenced line). The handler then persists the new emails as booking attendees (`attendees.createMany`) and triggers `sendAddGuestsEmails(...)`, which sends emails/ICS updates using the organizer identity (`from`/`replyTo` derive from `calEvent.organizer`). This enables an attendee to add arbitrary third-party emails as attendees, who then also satisfy `isAttendee` and can repeat the action, creating a self-propagating invitation/spam vector.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — guests array has no max length, so one request can insert thousands of attendee rows and fan out thousands of emails/ICS invites.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `addGuests` with input schema `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` (no `.max()`/size limit). The handler then does `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany({ data: guestsFullDetails }))` and calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which fans out emails over `calendarEvent.attendees.map(...)`. With no bounded array size, a single request can create a very large number of attendee rows and trigger a correspondingly large number of emails/ICS invites, enabling resource exhaustion/spam from an authenticated caller.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — Duplicate detection is a read-then-write check with no transaction or unique constraint, so concurrent addGuests calls double-insert the same guest.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code reads existing attendees (`prisma.booking.findFirst(... include: { attendees: true })`), computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering against that in-memory list, then performs a separate write with `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`. There is no transaction wrapping the read+write, and nothing in the diff shows a DB-level unique constraint being relied on, so two concurrent `addGuests` calls can both observe the same attendee as absent and both insert it via `createMany`, resulting in duplicate booking attendees (or a race-triggered failure if a unique constraint exists).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — Server never de-duplicates within the guests array itself, trusting the client-only zod refine, so repeated emails in one payload create duplicate attendees.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 — Existing-attendee comparison is case-sensitive, so a case-variant of an existing attendee's address is inserted as a brand-new duplicate attendee.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, uniqueGuests is computed with a case-sensitive check against existing attendees: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` and guests are not normalized (no `.toLowerCase()`). adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — Calendar attendee update runs unguarded after the DB write, so a provider failure leaves guests persisted but the external calendar out of sync with no rollback, retry, or compensating action.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the DB is updated first via prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...), then the external sync is attempted with `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` outside any transaction/try-catch. If the calendar provider call throws, the mutation will fail after guests are already persisted, leaving internal attendees updated but the external calendar unchanged, with no rollback/compensating action shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:80 — The operation is not retry-safe: after a mid-flight failure the guests already exist as attendees, so re-submitting filters them out and throws BAD_REQUEST, permanently blocking recovery of the skipped calendar/email side effects.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuestsHandler, the DB update (prisma.booking.update with attendees.createMany) happens before the calendar/email side effects (eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees and sendAddGuestsEmails). If a mid-flight failure occurs after the DB write (e.g., calendar update throws before emails, or process crashes), a retry will compute uniqueGuests by filtering out already-added attendees and then throws BAD_REQUEST when uniqueGuests.length===0, preventing re-running the skipped side effects. This non-idempotent ordering is visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:170 — The catch swallows the error and logs a bare string via console.log without the `err` object or logger context, so email failures are undiagnosable.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the `sendAddGuestsEmails` call is wrapped in `try/catch`, but the `catch (err)` only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and does not log `err` or any context. This doesn’t break functionality (the handler still returns success after updating attendees), but it makes email-send failures hard to diagnose and is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:120 — Promise.all over per-attendee getTranslation runs after the DB write and fails fast, so one translation load error aborts the handler with guests already persisted and no calendar/email sent.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the DB write happens first via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`, then `attendeesList` is built with `Promise.all(attendeesListPromises)` where each promise awaits `getTranslation(...)`. That `Promise.all` is not wrapped in a try/catch, so any single translation load rejection will throw and abort the handler after guests have already been persisted, and before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(...)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(...)` run. This can leave the system in a partially-updated state (guests stored but no calendar/email updates).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — sendAddGuestsEmails is passed the raw `guests` input instead of `uniqueGuests`, so pre-existing/blacklisted addresses are classified as new and get a full "scheduled" email.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code filters the input into `uniqueGuests` (excluding existing attendees and `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`) and only persists `uniqueGuests` via `createMany`. However it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw `guests` input. In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (email-manager.ts), the `newGuests` array is used to decide which attendees get a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` (`if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email)) ...`). Passing `guests` means pre-existing attendee emails included in the input (and any other excluded emails that already exist on the booking) will be misclassified as “new” and receive the full scheduled email instead of the add-guests update. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/email-manager.ts:549 — Promise.all fan-out over all recipient emails fails fast, so a single failed send masks the outcome of the remaining ones; Promise.allSettled with per-email logging is needed.

adjudication.rationale: In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (packages/emails/email-manager.ts), the diff shows `await Promise.all(emailsToSend);`. If any `sendEmail(...)` promise rejects, the awaited `Promise.all` rejects immediately, so the function stops awaiting the remaining sends and returns an error upstream. In the new handler (addGuests.handler.ts) that call is wrapped in a broad `try/catch` that only logs a generic message, so partial success/failure and which recipient failed is obscured. Switching to `Promise.allSettled` with per-email logging would improve robustness/observability, but the diff doesn’t prove a guaranteed functional break in all runtimes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — The external calendar call has no timeout or retry, so a hung/flaky provider stalls or fails the whole tRPC mutation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167 — Email delivery is done inline in the request path rather than queued as a background job, so transient SMTP failures are permanently lost and the user waits on N sends.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation awaits `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` directly in the request path (inside a `try/catch` that only logs on failure). This means the API response latency includes potentially many SMTP sends (`Promise.all` over organizer, team members, and attendees in `sendAddGuestsEmails`), and transient email failures are not retried/queued—errors are swallowed (`console.log`) and effectively lost. This is a concrete reliability/architecture concern introduced by the diff, though not a direct functional correctness bug in the booking update itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:58 — findFirstOrThrow on the organizer surfaces a raw Prisma error (opaque 500) instead of a typed TRPCError when booking.userId is null.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer is fetched via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is `null`/`undefined`, this coerces to `0`, and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw a Prisma error (not a `TRPCError`). There is no surrounding try/catch translating that into a typed `TRPCError`, so the API would surface an opaque 500 instead of a controlled error when `booking.userId` is missing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43 — The composed message is always truthy, making the `t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback dead code and surfacing raw error codes/untranslated keys to users.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` `onError`, `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` always produces a non-empty string (even when `err.data?.code` is undefined it becomes e.g. `"undefined: ..."`). Therefore `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` will never hit the fallback, making it dead code and potentially surfacing raw error codes and untranslated `err.message` keys to users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:40 — utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate() is not awaited inside the async onSuccess, so a rejected invalidation is an unhandled rejection and the list may show stale data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46 — Wrong boolean combinator: `isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner` should be `||`, so the team-permission branch is broken (admins denied, and the intent of the check is not what is enforced).

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner to pass the team-permission branch. Given the variable name and typical authorization semantics, this likely should be an OR check; as written it will incorrectly deny users who are only admins (or only owners) and make the permission gate stricter than intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — Blacklist bypass: env list is lowercased but the submitted guest email is not, so `Spam@Example.com` slips past `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the blacklist is normalized to lowercase (`BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(...).map(email => email.toLowerCase())`), but the submitted `guest` strings are compared without normalization: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Since `guests` comes from input (`z.array(z.string().email())`) and is not lowercased in the handler, a mixed/upper-cased email like `Spam@Example.com` will not match a lowercased blacklist entry (`spam@example.com`) and will pass the filter, effectively bypassing the blacklist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52 — Any attendee (a mere guest, matched only by email) can add unlimited arbitrary guests to someone else's booking, escalating a guest into a booking mutator.

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` explicitly authorizes any logged-in user whose email matches any existing booking attendee: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and then permits mutation if `isAttendee` is true (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw ...`). There is no additional role/ownership check beyond email match, and no cap on `guests` array length in `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` or the handler, so an attendee can add arbitrary numbers of new guests to a booking they don’t own.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — No rate limiting or cap on `guests.length`, so one authenticated user can blast unlimited attacker-controlled addresses with booking emails (spam amplification from the platform's domain).

adjudication.rationale: Verified: `addGuests` accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no upper bound in `addGuests.schema.ts`, and `addGuests.handler.ts` does not cap `guests.length` or implement throttling before calling `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. Since `sendAddGuestsEmails` fans out emails to organizer/team plus `calendarEvent.attendees.map(...)`, an authenticated caller can submit a very large `guests` array and trigger a large volume of outbound emails (spam amplification) from the platform.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:26 — Booking is fetched by id with no status/time filter, so guests can be added to CANCELLED/REJECTED/past bookings, triggering CONFIRMED ICS invites and emails.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the booking is fetched only by `id` (`prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... })`) with no checks on booking status (e.g., cancelled/rejected) or timing (e.g., already ended). The handler then unconditionally updates calendar attendees and sends add-guests emails/invites. The new email templates explicitly generate ICS payloads with `status: "CONFIRMED"` (`packages/emails/templates/*-add-guests-email.ts`), so calling this on a cancelled/rejected booking would send conflicting CONFIRMED invites/emails. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — eventType.disableGuests` (and seated-event guest restrictions) are never checked, bypassing the organizer's opt-out of guests.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation unconditionally appends new `attendees` via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` after only checking user permission (team admin/owner, organizer, or existing attendee). Although `booking.eventType` is included in the initial query, there is no conditional gate that consults any event-type-level guest restrictions (e.g., an `eventType.disableGuests` flag) or seated-event constraints before allowing guests to be added. If such restrictions exist, this endpoint would bypass them and still add guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — Raw `guests` input rather than `uniqueGuests` is passed to the email sender, so already-existing attendees supplied by the caller get a full AttendeeScheduledEmail re-disclosing booking details on demand.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler filters caller input into `uniqueGuests` (excluding emails already in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted ones) and only persists `uniqueGuests`. However it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw `guests` input (not `uniqueGuests`). In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` controls whether an attendee gets `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`, so an existing attendee email included by the caller will be misclassified as “new” and receive a full scheduled email again. Passing `uniqueGuests` would align email behavior with the actual added guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — Calendar update uses the *caller's* credentials (`ctx.user`) instead of the booking organizer's, so a team admin/attendee action writes with the wrong account's third-party credentials.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is executed via `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })` where `user` is `ctx.user` (the caller) and `credentials` are fetched with `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. Since the mutation explicitly allows non-organizers to add guests (`isTeamAdminOrOwner` / `isAttendee`), this can cause `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` to run using the caller’s third-party credentials rather than the booking organizer’s, which is likely incorrect and can break updates or write to the wrong external calendar account.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:80 — Distinct BAD_REQUEST when every submitted address is already an attendee lets a caller probe whether a specific email is on the booking.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler filters submitted `guests` down to `uniqueGuests` by removing existing attendees and blacklisted emails. If `uniqueGuests.length === 0` it throws `TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" })`. This creates an oracle: an authorized caller can submit a single non-blacklisted email and distinguish “already an attendee” (BAD_REQUEST) from “not an attendee” (mutation proceeds), allowing probing of whether a specific email is on the booking.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts:25 — replyTo` includes every attendee email, leaking the full attendee list to each team member recipient.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the email payload sets `replyTo` to an array containing the organizer email plus every attendee email: `replyTo: [this.calEvent.organizer.email, ...this.calEvent.attendees.map(({ email }) => email)]`. Since `to` is set to each team member (`toAddresses = [this.teamMember?.email || this.calEvent.organizer.email]`), each team member recipient will receive an email whose Reply-To header exposes the full attendee list, which is a privacy/security leak as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — Schema lacks max array length / dedupe / lowercase normalization, leaving server-side validation weaker than the client dialog's.

adjudication.rationale: The server schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only enforces `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no dedupe/normalization/limits, while the client dialog additionally refines for uniqueness.
